1	# Supporting Kokoro and Phonon with their voices
     2	
     3	The settled decisions are in `decisions.md`, numbered in the order the user settled them. The spike's measurements are in `spikes/phonon-vs-kokoro/findings.md`. The canvas `canvas/explore.tldr.json` and its export `canvas/explore.svg` hold the diagrams below with their source notes.
     4	
     5	## Today (code at a2a68b1)
     6	
     7	An item carries one voice, a free-text string. The client sends it to `POST /items`, or `pickVoice` in `api/src/voices.ts` picks one at random from 10 Kokoro ids. The API stores it in `items.voice` (NOT NULL, no default, no CHECK), the pipeline sends it unchanged in Modal's `/start` request, and every poll returns it. No code outside `tts/` names a model. The Modal app `nagara-tts` hard-codes Kokoro (`KPipeline(lang_code="a")` on an L4), and the pipeline prices every item with one global `ttsDollarsPerSecond`. Nothing validates the voice, so an unknown voice fails inside Modal. Details with file and line references are in `scout-voice-flow.md`, and the docs' current statements about the voice and the model are in `docs-voice.md`.
     8	
     9	## Proposed data model
    10	
    11	| Part | Change | Decisions |
    12	|---|---|---|
    13	| `items.model` | New column, an enum `"kokoro" \| "phonon"` with a CHECK, like `status`. The migration sets `"kokoro"` on existing rows. | 13, 24, 29 |
    14	| `items.voice` | The voice is always one of the item's model's voices. | 14, 20 |
    15	| TTS catalog in `common/` | New. Each model's voices and default voice, and the default model. Kokoro: its American voices (`af_*`, `am_*`), default `af_heart`. Phonon: its 12 American voices, default `Zoey`. Default model: Kokoro. | 18, 23, 25, 27, 28 |
    16	| Enqueue body | Gains `model?`. The API applies the default model, then the model's default voice, and answers 400 when the voice does not belong to the model. No random pick. | 15, 16, 20 |
    17	| `VOICE_POOL` and `pickVoice` | Removed. | 20 |
    18	| Item response | Carries `model` next to `voice`, on `GET /items/:id` and on the enqueue response, which uses the same `toItemResponse`. | 22 |
    19	| Modal `/start` request | Gains `model`. One app spawns the matching class: Kokoro on an L4, Phonon on 1 CPU core with `ptts==0.4.1`, both with `scaledown_window=300` and a snapshot. One `MODAL_START_URL` stays. | 12, 26, 30, 31 |
    20	| Cost row | The row keeps its shape. `dollars` is the audio seconds times the model's rate, with the rates in the pipeline's config: Kokoro about 0.0000084 and Phonon about 0.0000028 dollars per audio second (warm compute only). | 17, 21 |
    21

    24	    participant C as Client

    27	    participant P as Pipeline Worker

    35	        A->>D: insert item (model, voice)
    36	        A-->>C: item

    38	    P->>D: read item.model, item.voice
    39	    P->>M: /start {paragraphs, model, voice, destination}
    40	    M-->>P: format, duration, timings
    41	    P->>D: audio fields + tts cost (duration x rate of model)
    42	    C->>A: GET /items/:id
    43	    A-->>C: model?, voice, audio_url
    44	```
    45	
    46	## Code the change touches
    47	
    48	- `common/src/db/schema.ts` and a generated migration for `items.model` (invariant 7); `createItem` and `ItemRow` gain the model.
    49	- `api/src/routes/enqueue.ts`: the valibot body, the defaults and the voice check. The catalog in `common/` replaces `api/src/voices.ts`.
    50	- `pipeline/src/workflow/steps/synthesis.ts` and `pipeline/src/tts/modal.ts`: the start request carries the model, and the store step prices with the model's rate. `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc` holds one rate per model.
    51	- `tts/app.py`: a Phonon class next to Kokoro, `StartRequest` gains the model, and `StartRequest.voice` loses its `af_heart` default, because the API now always sends a voice.
    52	- Tests: about 7 fixtures with `af_heart`, `api/test/enqueue.test.ts` (it duplicates `VOICE_POOL` and requests `bf_emma`, which decisions 14, 16 and 18 now reject), and the Modal fake in `pipeline/test/helpers/services.ts`.
    53	- Docs (decision 19): `product-design/queue.md` ("Voices"), `technical-design/item-contract.md`, `item-lifecycle.md`, `tts-service.md`, `persistence-and-storage.md` and `product-design/what-nagara-is.md`.
    54

    56	
    57	- Whether redeploying the Modal app after a change to one class discards the other class's snapshot (in decision 26 the user chose not to run the spike that would answer it).
    58	- The spike's full-article timings and Whisper check used the Phonon voice Hadley, not the default Zoey.

2	     2	
3	     3	The settled decisions are in `decisions.md`, numbered in the order the user settled them. The spike's measurements are in `spikes/phonon-vs-kokoro/findings.md`. The canvas `canvas/explore.tldr.json` and its export `canvas/explore.svg` hold the diagrams below with their source notes.

5	     5	## Today (code at a2a68b1)
6	     6	
7	     7	An item carries one voice, a free-text string. The client sends it to `POST /items`, or `pickVoice` in `api/src/voices.ts` picks one at random from 10 Kokoro ids. The API stores it in `items.voice` (NOT NULL, no default, no CHECK), the pipeline sends it unchanged in Modal's `/start` request, and every poll returns it. No code outside `tts/` names a model. The Modal app `nagara-tts` hard-codes Kokoro (`KPipeline(lang_code="a")` on an L4), and the pipeline prices every item with one global `ttsDollarsPerSecond`. Nothing validates the voice, so an unknown voice fails inside Modal. Details with file and line references are in `scout-voice-flow.md`, and the docs' current statements about the voice and the model are in `docs-voice.md`.
